## Summary

Deep case study of how far this calculator is from "every competitor plus scientific prose in any language", with executable corpora, an automated gap checker, and the full work plan filed as 18 sub-issues (#229 to #246) with GitHub blocker dependencies.

- `scripts/competitor-coverage.mjs` runs every corpus row through the one-shot CLI and classifies it as `supported`, `different`, `unsupported` or `timeout`; writes `results/coverage-report.md` and a compact `coverage-baseline.json`; `--baseline` fails on regressions. Unit-tested by `scripts/competitor-coverage.test.mjs` (runs in the existing `node --test scripts/*.test.mjs` CI step).
- `scripts/import-competitor-corpus.mjs` extracts single-expression assertions from the fend, libqalculate, Numbat, Rink and math.js test suites (2550 rows, upstream licenses cited in the file header).
- `docs/case-studies/issue-227/`: README with requirement inventory, method, measurements, error classes, solution options, component evaluation and dependency graph; `competitor-inventory.md`; `natural-language-corpus.md`; three corpora (3055 rows); the generated report and baseline; the 18 sub-issue bodies exactly as filed plus `issues.json`.
